numerical_failure.observed_behavior: For float16 input, np.sinc(float16(0)) returns a wrong value because the fill value 1.0e-20 underflows float16 when substituted for zero before computing sin(y)/y, so the division yields an invalid/incorrect result instead of the correct limit of 1.
numerical_failure.expected_behavior: np.sinc(float16(0)) should return the correct value (1 at x=0) without underflow; the zero fill value should be the smallest normal of np.float64 (or the finfo eps of the input dtype for float kinds) rather than 1e-20, so float16 inputs no longer produce an incorrect result.

the zero-replacement constant 1.0e-20 underflows to zero in float16
the call is numpy.sinc(x) where x == 0 exactly, so where(x == 0, 1.0e-20, x) is used
